name: How Long Does ADU Construction Take in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical ADU construction project take in Los Angeles County from design to final inspection?
mainEntity.text: How long does a typical ADU construction project take in Los Angeles County from design to final inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most ADU projects take longer than homeowners expect because the schedule includes more than just construction. A realistic timeline usually starts with design and feasibility checks, followed by permit plan preparation, city review, revisions, procurement, construction, and final inspections. In Los Angeles County, the biggest schedule risks are incomplete plans, structural changes, utility relocations, soil or grading issues, and delays in permit review. Detached ADUs, garage conversions, and addition-style ADUs each follow different timelines because site work and utility requirements vary. To reduce delays, confirm zoning constraints early, finalize the layout before submission, and ask the contractor for a schedule that separates pre-construction, permitting, and build phases. A good contractor should also identify long-lead items such as windows, cabinets, electrical panels, and HVAC equipment before work begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: A typical ADU project in Los Angeles County can take several months from design through permitting, construction, and final inspection. The timeline depends on plan complexity, utility upgrades, site conditions, and permit review speed. Projects move faster when drawings are complete, scope is fixed early, and the contractor coordinates inspections and subcontractors efficiently.
